result.summary: Adds an `-ipcconnect` option to `bitcoin-gui` in multiprocess builds, allowing the GUI to connect over IPC to an existing `bitcoin-node` process instead of spawning a new child node subprocess. Defaults to `-ipcconnect=auto`, which attempts to connect to `<datadir>/sockets/node.sock` if present and falls back to spawning a node if not.
result.problem: In multiprocess builds, `bitcoin-gui` spawns and manages its own dedicated `bitcoin-node` subprocess, which terminates when the GUI is closed. Users cannot keep a persistent node daemon running in the background and attach or detach GUI sessions on demand.
evidence: PR description: 'Building on #10102, this adds an -ipcconnect option to bitcoin-gui that connects the GUI to an existing bitcoin-node process already running in the background instead of spawning a new bitcoin-node process. This allows the GUI to be started and stopped independently of the node.'
Part of the process separation project (#28722).
result.scope_notes: This is a stacked PR of 30 commits where 29 commits belong to upstream dependencies (#10102, #19460, #29409) and subtree updates. Only the single final commit (34bb890839) is unique to this pull request. The feature is inactive unless built with `--enable-multiprocess`.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased onto updated base branches, picking up the latest libmultiprocess subtree v14 update and btcsignals eager-destruction fixes. The unique payload commit remains the same.
result.card: Adds an -ipcconnect command-line option to bitcoin-gui, allowing it to connect over IPC to an existing background bitcoin-node process rather than spawning a dedicated node subprocess. By default (-ipcconnect=auto), the GUI checks for a socket at sockets/node.sock and connects to it, falling back to spawning a new node process if not present. This enables users of experimental multiprocess builds to start and stop GUI instances independently without shutting down the node. The PR is part of the process separation project (#28722) and is stacked on #10102, #19460, and #29409, containing only a single unique commit.

risk.why: Changes only take effect in experimental multiprocess builds (--enable-multiprocess) when running the GUI binary, with zero effect on standard monolithic builds.
